result: Wild-type fission yeast cells have approximately 190 single cytokinesis nodes early in mitosis, with single node fluorescence intensity of 2300 ± 900 AU following a normal distribution. About 85% of these nodes are incorporated into contractile rings.
evaluation: Claims C3, C49, C50, and C51 are well-supported by Airyscan microscopy measurements, statistical validation (Shapiro-Wilk test, Z-score), and quantitative fluorescence analysis shown in Figures 2D and 2E. The methodology for counting nodes by dividing total fluorescence by average single node intensity is sound, and the statistical tests confirm the normal distribution assumption.

result: The number of cytokinesis nodes scales linearly with cell volume (slope ~0.7 nodes/µm³) across multiple strains with varying cell sizes, but does not correlate with cell diameter. The rga4Δ mutant cells deviate from this trend with fewer nodes than expected for their volume.
evaluation: Claims C5, C59-C63 are supported by linear regression analysis (p<0.0001, R²=0.5) across 125 cells from multiple strains shown in Figure 3H-I. The deviation of rga4Δ cells is documented and the lack of correlation with diameter (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B) strengthens the volume-specific relationship. Statistical significance is properly reported.

result: The local concentration of Pom1 at the plasma membrane in the broad band region does not vary significantly across cells with different sizes and node numbers, indicating that local Pom1 concentration does not control cytokinesis node number during the G2/M transition.
evaluation: Claims C8, C70-C72 are supported by quantitative measurements across five strains with fivefold size variation (Figure 4C-D) showing no significant correlation (p=0.07, R²=0.03). The linear regression analysis properly demonstrates the lack of relationship between local Pom1 concentration and node number.

result: Artificially varying total cellular Pom1 concentration using the nmt81 promoter increases cell length, local Pom1 concentration at the membrane, and cytokinesis node number above the baseline of ~190, while single node intensity and broad band width remain constant. This results in higher node density and a smaller fractional broad band width.
evaluation: Claims C10, C73-C82 are supported by systematic measurements across different Pom1 expression levels (Figure 5). Linear regressions show significant correlations for cell length (p<0.0001, R²=0.5), membrane Pom1 (p<0.0001, R²=0.7), and node number (p=0.0017, R²=0.3), while broad band width shows no correlation (p=0.3). The experimental design using the nmt81 promoter is appropriate.

result: Artificially increasing total cellular Cdr2 concentration reduces cell length at division but does not change broad band width, resulting in increased node numbers above the basal level of ~190 and higher node density.
evaluation: Claims C83-C87, C89 are supported by measurements using the nmt81 promoter system (Figure 6). Significant correlations are shown for cell length (p<0.0001, R²=0.6) and node number (p<0.0001, R²=0.6), while broad band width shows no correlation (p=0.9). The conclusion that Cdr2 can drive node numbers above baseline is justified by the data.

result: Airyscan microscopy with ~140 nm resolution resolves dim single cytokinesis nodes better than conventional confocal microscopy, producing brighter and narrower images of contractile rings and retrieving higher spatial frequencies.
evaluation: Claims C43-C46 are supported by direct comparison between Airyscan and confocal imaging (Figure 1) and Fast Fourier transform analysis showing superior frequency retrieval. The technical specifications of Airyscan are well-established, and the visual and quantitative comparisons validate the improved resolution.

result: In freely cycling cells (excluding cdc25-22), both node density and broad band width increase with node number and cell size. In contrast, cdc25-22 mutant cells expand broad band width proportionally to node number without increasing density.
evaluation: Claims C64, C65, C108 are supported by data in Figure 3J-K showing different scaling behaviors. The distinction between cdc25-22 and other strains is clearly documented with appropriate statistical analysis. The mechanistic explanation for cdc25-22 behavior (arrested at G2/M) is reasonable.

result: Different strains incorporate varying fractions of Blt1 from cytokinesis nodes into contractile rings (40-90%), with cdc25-22 mutant cells showing particularly low incorporation (~50% in largest cells) for Blt1 but normal incorporation for Myo2.
evaluation: Claims C66-C69, C120-C121 are supported by fluorescence measurements in Figure 3—figure supplement 2 and Figure 2E. The differential incorporation of Blt1 vs Myo2 in cdc25-22 cells is a novel observation properly documented with quantitative data. Statistical significance is established (p=0.035 for wild-type comparison).

result: Temperature-sensitive mutants and deletion mutants produce cells with altered dimensions: wee1-50 cells are half the length of wild-type; cdc25-22 cells are twice as long; rga4Δ cells are shorter but wider; rga2Δ cells are narrower but normal length.
evaluation: Claims C52-C57 are supported by quantitative measurements in Figure 3 and are consistent with known functions of these genes. The measurements include appropriate sample sizes and standard deviations. These phenotypes are well-established in the literature and properly reproduced here.

result: Cell size is the dominant determinant of the basal number of cytokinesis nodes (~190 in wild-type), with Pom1 and Cdr2 modulating this number through their effects on cell size during interphase and their concentrations during mitosis.
evaluation: Claims C90, C91, C94, C95 represent the central mechanistic model supported by the scaling data (Figure 3H), the Pom1/Cdr2 manipulation experiments (Figures 5-6), and integration with prior literature. The model is consistent with all experimental observations and properly distinguishes basal from modulated node numbers.

result: Pom1 regulates node localization and cell size through a phosphorylation cascade: Pom1 phosphorylates and inhibits Cdr2 (affecting oligomerization and membrane binding), Cdr2 phosphorylates and inhibits Wee1, and Wee1 phosphorylates Cdk1. As cells grow, Pom1's influence diminishes, contributing to mitotic entry.
evaluation: Claims C96-C100 are well-supported by multiple citations to prior work establishing this pathway. The current study's observations of Pom1 distribution (Figure 4) and effects of Pom1 overexpression (Figure 5) are consistent with this established mechanism. This represents integration of prior knowledge with new observations.

result: Overexpression of Cdr2 increases node numbers by mass action and promotes premature mitosis through Wee1 inhibition, resulting in short cells with densely packed nodes. Overexpression of Pom1 delays mitosis allowing cells to grow longer, with the dominant effect of cell size producing more nodes despite Cdr2 inhibition.
evaluation: Claims C101-C104, C112 represent mechanistic interpretations of the experimental data (Figures 5-6) but are largely speculative. While the observations are solid, the proposed mechanisms involving 'mass action' and the relative contributions of different pathways are not directly tested. The authors appropriately use tentative language ('might', 'may'), but these remain hypotheses requiring further validation.

result: During interphase growth in wild-type cells, the Pom1 concentration remains low in a widening zone at the cell middle, while node density and number increase with cell size (except in cdc25-22 cells), and the broad band widens proportionally.
evaluation: Claims C105-C107 are supported by the scaling data (Figure 3J-K), Pom1 distribution measurements (Figure 4C), and integration with prior literature (Bhatia et al., 2014; Pan et al., 2014). The observations extend previous findings to a wider range of cell sizes and are internally consistent.

result: Cell shape influences node number, with large-diameter rga4Δ cells having fewer nodes than expected for their volume despite normal node properties. These cells also show a steeper Pom1 gradient and wider Blt1 distribution.
evaluation: Claims C115-C117 are supported by the deviation of rga4Δ cells from the volume-node number relationship (Figure 3H) and the Pom1 distribution data (Figure 4B). The observation is well-documented, though the mechanistic explanation remains incomplete. This represents a genuine exception to the volume-scaling rule.

result: Background on cytokinesis node biology: nodes are stoichiometric protein assemblies that serve as contractile ring precursors, form from two types of interphase nodes, mature by sequential protein accumulation, and are linked to cell size control.
evaluation: Claims C1-C2, C11-C24 represent established background knowledge properly cited from prior literature. These claims provide essential context but are not novel findings of this study. The citations are appropriate and the descriptions are accurate based on the referenced work.

result: Prior studies using various microscopy techniques estimated cytokinesis node numbers ranging from <50 to ~140, with limitations including inability to detect dim nodes, resolution constraints, and reliance on extrapolation. SMLM revealed that nodes are uniform in size but appear heterogeneous in confocal images due to clustering.
evaluation: Claims C25-C40 accurately summarize prior literature on node counting methods and their limitations. The citations are appropriate and the critical assessment of previous methods (including their own prior work) is fair and well-documented. This provides essential justification for the current study's approach.

result: Blt1 is the only protein that persists in nodes throughout the cell cycle, making it suitable as a marker. Time-lapse imaging shows nodes of all sizes condense into contractile rings over 10-12 minutes, but neither Airyscan nor confocal microscopy can resolve individual nodes within rings.
evaluation: Claims C42, C47, C48 are supported by citations for Blt1's unique properties and by the imaging data. The limitation regarding resolution of nodes in rings is appropriately acknowledged and consistent with the known resolution limits of these techniques compared to SMLM.

result: Single node fluorescence intensity is consistent (~2300 AU) across wild-type and all experimental strains tested.
evaluation: Claim C58 is supported by the histogram data in Figure 3G showing similar distributions across strains. Tukey's multiple comparison test confirms no significant differences (p>0.05) except for rga4Δ+HU (p=0.04), which is a minor deviation. This validates the use of a common single-node intensity for node counting across strains.

result: Only about half of each known node protein assembles into nodes, and cells lacking either Cdr2 or Pom1 can still form cytokinesis nodes, indicating a basal node-forming capacity independent of these kinases.
evaluation: Claims C92-C93 are supported by appropriate citations (Akamatsu et al., 2017 for C92; multiple citations for C93). These observations from prior work are correctly interpreted to support the concept of a basal node number that can be modulated by Pom1 and Cdr2.

result: Two additional factors contribute to restricting nodes to the equator: an uncharacterized activity that excludes nodes from one pole in pom1Δ cells, and anillin Mid1, as mid1Δ cells have nodes spread over the entire plasma membrane.
evaluation: Claims C109-C110 are supported by appropriate citations to prior work. These represent known but incompletely understood aspects of node localization that complement the Pom1-mediated restriction mechanism. The citations are accurate and relevant.

result: In arrested cdc25-22 cells that continue growing, extra nodes formed after the threshold time spread out further from the edges of the broad band.
evaluation: Claim C111 is a speculative explanation for why cdc25-22 cells show different scaling behavior (expanding broad band width rather than increasing density). While this interpretation is reasonable given the experimental design (cells arrested at G2/M), it is not directly demonstrated. The claim represents inference rather than direct observation.

result: Cells overexpressing Pom1 have higher node density due to more nodes in normal-width broad bands, with increased Pom1 concentration in the cell middle suppressing broad band spreading despite increased cell length.
evaluation: Claims C113-C114 are supported by the data in Figures 5F-G showing constant broad band width with increased node numbers, and Figure 5B showing increased local Pom1 concentration. The observations are internally consistent and properly documented.

result: Most cytokinesis node proteins are initially incorporated into contractile rings, with Myo2 retained and concentrated while Mid1 and actin are lost during constriction. The observation that nodes in rings have different compositions than cytokinesis nodes suggests compositional changes during ring maturation.
evaluation: Claims C118-C119 are supported by appropriate citations to prior work. Claim C122 is a reasonable inference from the new observation that Blt1 and Myo2 show different incorporation patterns (Figure 3—figure supplement 2), suggesting that ring nodes differ from cytokinesis nodes. This inference is logical but requires further validation.
